records.title: Arrival and an enquiry about the situation
records.header_literal: A) CZ v CM (20.00 p.m., November 12th); 20.00; RIZI-64
records.readable_german: Gut angekommen. Ist dort was los. SEIF.
records.meaning: The sender reports having arrived safely and asks whether anything is happening at the other end. The closing SEIF is retained as an abbreviated label; this short message does not itself give a location or establish a full personal identity.
notes: All 64 native coordinates decode directly under the unchanged key, with no changes or source-mask fills. The following NF CM UM transmission-control text is outside the 64-coordinate body.
The wording IST DORT WAS LOS is a question. The readable quotation uses a period so that a question mark remains reserved for an unresolved plaintext position in this edition.
SEIF is not expanded to a full name in the exact readable quotation.
source_rows: DDDDX XVGAG DDVGG FVDAD DXFXA GGDVV AGXDA GXGVV GVDAD AVAXD DDDDA DDXDX AVAG

records.title: Request for notification when Seifert has arrived
records.header_literal: B) CM v CZ (18.54 p.m., November 12th); 19.10; RIZI-74
records.readable_german: Wenn Seifert eingetroffen, bitte NACHR. TOF.
records.meaning: The message asks for notification when Seifert has arrived. NACHR is read as an abbreviated request for news or a message. TOF remains a closing label with no claimed personal or station identity.
notes: The native body contains 74 occupied slots, including literal Z at source indices4 and31, W at42, and five B glyphs at60–64. These eight invalid coordinate glyphs remain in the transcription and become eight separately priced analysis-mask fills.

The proposal changes no observed ADFGVX coordinate. The five B-shaped slots are filled with D coordinates; this is an explicit source-mask completion, not a silent claim that five clearly printed Ds were present.
The source ending CZ UM is transmission control after the 74-slot ciphertext and is excluded from the body on that printed framing.
NACHR and TOF remain abbreviated or literal; no sender biography is supplied.

The earlier p174 B witness supplies all eight invalid-glyph values here, while this source supplies D at p174 source20, supporting its previously unresolved N in EINGETROFFEN. Under conservative masks all74 source coordinates and all37 target pairs have an observed witness, with zero observed-coordinate conflicts.

If the earlier C/G-like glyph is instead treated as an observed G, the complete-word proposal costs one observed substitution in that alternative. The new D witness does not change the appearance of the old glyph.
source_rows: DVFVZ DFXFD ADAAF XFFDX DVXXF XAVAA AZXVA VVVVA DAWDV AXFFV XDXVD FDDXA BBBBB XXXDD VDVD

records.title: A report that Seifert has departed
records.header_literal: C) CM v CZ (17.26 p.m., November 12th); 18.20; RIZI-46
records.meaning: The proposed reading reports that Seifert has departed. RENTE is the literal closing field; the record alone does not identify it as a particular person or station.
notes: All 46 printed coordinates are retained, including the final six FFVDD V omitted from the earlier OCR body. The following CZ is outside the ciphertext.
The source produces SQIFERT directly. The proposal SEIFERT changes one observed coordinate; the neighboring arrival enquiry supports the name but does not make this change free.
The full 46-slot ciphertext is preserved; no historical prefix or suffix is invented.

Compared with existing p174 E, this source supports E at plaintext4 through observed source2 X instead of G. Both witnesses still have Q at plaintext1, so SEIFERT requires one additional word correction in each witness there. The combined edited cost is3 substitutions versus1 unavoidable observed-source conflict; the extra2 are contextual name repairs.

records.title: An enquiry about the car
records.header_literal: E) CM v CZ (17.12 p.m., November 12th); 17.40; RIZI-36
records.meaning: The message asks where the car is or why it has not arrived. The closing KRAMM is preserved without assigning a biography or a vehicle. The text is an enquiry, not proof that a car was sent.
notes: The source supplies all 36 coordinates and decrypts directly, with no coordinate changes or mask fills.
The nearby D record is a similar but differently framed printed witness. It is not silently substituted for this complete E body.
The interrogative sentence is displayed with a period to reserve ? for unresolved plaintext positions.

prior_credit: Published period keys: George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker (2016), and George Lasry (2017 key list). Earlier repository OCR and unchanged-key outputs are retained separately. Source review and explicit editorial work: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro. No universal first-decipherment priority is asserted. The arrival-enquiry and departure wording was already presented for p174 B/E in cases/radio/seifert.md. The new p183 witnesses add coordinate support and a separately priced comparison, not a new claim to that wording or extra message groups.
limits: All native source slots remain in printed order; no insertion, deletion or reordering.
Unknown square cells remain globally coupled and injective. Roundtrip completion witnesses are explicitly nonhistorical.
Observed-coordinate substitutions and source-mask fills are priced separately. A source-compatible word proposal is not proof of unique historical wording.
